gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-orbit: Sleek and slightly sci-fi, Neuropol keeps its letters closed and tight with a slim channel cut into the c. Orbit is the looser one, curves stopping short of closing and each character floating apart, so it does the quiet, spaced-out work.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-science-gothic: Futuristic from the first letter, Neuropol draws its shapes with a single-weight outline feel and a slim channel in the c. Science Gothic then spreads its stroke ends far apart, so you take in one letter at a time under that closed, tight heading.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-syncopate: Neuropol has a digital, outlined look, with closed letters and a slim channel where the c opens. Syncopate follows in open shapes drawn with a technical-pen steadiness, its spacing like rungs on a rope ladder, so a long passage would feel measured and steady.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-abeezee: Words that look pulled apart letter by letter, glowing like neon tubes, set the tone in Neuropolitical. ABeeZee sits beneath it with terminals finishing well clear of the stem and a mean line set high, a friendly, quiet plain sans next to all that glow.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-aldrich: Neuropolitical lights up its headings with neon-tube letters and big open counters in every small letter. Aldrich takes the other job, its x-height close to the cap height and round letters cupped rather than clenched, like tracing a single thick thread.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-alexandria: Alexandria is a tall-bodied sans-serif with wide open c terminals and short stems above and below. Neuropolitical meets it with curves and stems in lockstep, so the glowing, tube-like heading sits over a lower, quieter text.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-amiko: Amiko reads modern and plain, its lowercase strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark and its terminals pointing outward like tongs. And Neuropolitical gives it a foil, with no calligraphic swell on any downstroke, just glowing neon-tube lines.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-anek-bangla: Neuropolitical looks pulled apart letter by letter, a neon tube with no thick-thin modulation at all. And Anek Bangla feels closer and friendlier beside it, with wide s curves barely curled in and a short stretch from midline to ascender.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-anek-devana: Contemporary and geometric, Neuropolitical glows in neon-tube letters whose stroke ends are as wide as the middle. Anek Devanagari does the quieter work, with distinctly open letter mouths and a tall middle zone in its sans-serif shapes.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-anek-gujara: Neuropolitical looks like bent rope or glowing tubing, its words pulled apart letter by letter. Anek Gujarati would read easily beneath it, with lowercase that rivals the capitals and a gaping c opening that keeps a sans line open.
